newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Drnovsek fails to win over right.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Drnovsek fails to win over right.

text.p: Slovenian prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek on Friday failed to broker a deal with right-wing parties to form a new coalition government, a conservative party chief told national radio.

Marjan Podobnik, leader of the conservative People's Party, said the differences between Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats and an alliance of three rightist parties were too great and no agreement could be found.

"At the last meeting today we found out that in spite of trying to set up a government of national unity, it is not possible," Podobnik told Slovenian radio. "The differences among the parties are too big."
Podobnik heads the so-called "Spring" alliance, comprising his People's Party, the centre-right Social Democrats and the Christian Democrats, who together hold 44 seats in the 90-member parliament.

Drnovsek, who has attempted to set up a wide coalition, could still command a majority of one in parliament after winning support from ex-communists, the leftist Desus party and the Nationalist Party.
Drnovsek has held talks over the past two weeks to form a government after weeks of political deadlock which followed an inconclusive general election on November 10.
